title: Fix CROSSSLOT and nuanced multi-key behavior under a clustered policy
intent: Checks the answer explains CROSSSLOT under a clustered policy, applies hash-tag colocation, and defers nuanced multi-key multi-slot behavior to the enterprise data plane rather than the OSS assumption.
prompt: Review this clustered Azure Managed Redis access pattern and correct the multi-key operations.

input_artifacts.name: access-pattern.txt
input_artifacts.content: policy=clustered; keys: cart:{userA}, coupon:{promoX}, inventory:{skuY}; op: MGET across all three; also a Lua script mutating all three atomically; assumption: 'multi-key commands always work across the cluster'

embedded_defects.defect: MGET and a Lua script span keys on different slots and will hit CROSSSLOT.
No shared hash tag colocates the co-accessed keys.
Assumes generic OSS multi-key behavior instead of what the enterprise data plane enforces.
